newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-up $0.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-up $0.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices were called steady to $0.50 per cwt higher Friday as several meat packers may need hogs for Saturday slaughter, livestock dealers said.
Profitable slaughter margins and holiday-reduced operations next week has several packers scheduling Saturday slaughter operations, sources said.
Hog marketings should be adequate Friday, following slightly reduced runs Thursday because of snow- and ice-slickened roads from Minnesota to Ohio.
"Unless the weather gets bad, we should have a decent run (Friday)," said an Illinois dealer.
Hogs traded mostly $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher Thursday because of higher pork prices this past week and meat packers preparing for Saturday slaughter operations.
